title: What's trending on the internet this week? The 6 trends people searched (Nov 9–15, 2026)
answer: This week the internet was busy with "Microsoft 364" jokes after a major outage, an ironic meme about Finland's embassy in Canberra closing for a day, the hunt for Fortnite's ultra-rare Pirate Coin, Kasane Teto's arrival in Fortnite, the "Remember November 2026" polar bear, and a nationwide FAA ground stop.
body:
How we built this list: from our trend radar's data, which tracks new Google search suggestions, Reddit, Know Your Meme and other sources, and then checked each trend against at least two reliable sources.

1. Microsoft 364. On Thursday, Nov. 12, Outlook, Teams and other Microsoft 365 apps went down for many users around the world, and people renamed the service "Microsoft 364" for the day it lost. Microsoft said a network change caused the problem, not a hack, and services recovered on Nov. 13. Full explainer: https://trendrundown.com/x/what-does-microsoft-364-mean

2. The Embassy of Finland in Canberra. A routine Instagram notice that the embassy would close on Nov. 10 for a staff day became a worldwide in-joke, with people pretending the closure ruined their week. Other Finnish missions, airlines and even Finland's president joined in. Full explainer: https://trendrundown.com/x/embassy-of-finland-canberra-meme

3. The Fortnite Pirate Coin. Fortnite's One Piece crossover mini-season, which began Nov. 1, added a "Pirate Shop Access" coin that Epic says drops from about 1 in 137,500 chests. Finding one unlocks two 14-day windows of free Item Shop items, so players flooded TikTok with videos of endless chest hunts and fake "I found it" clips. The coin can only drop until the mini-season ends on Dec. 5.

4. Kasane Teto in Fortnite. On Nov. 12, the virtual singer Kasane Teto arrived in Fortnite as part of a Music Mini-Pass that costs 1,000 V-Bucks. Teto began as an April Fools' prank on a Japanese message board on April 1, 2008, and later became a real singing-synthesizer voice. Longtime fans argued about the debut, especially a back bling showing her face on a pear, a fan joke called "Pearto."

5. "Remember November 2026." An eerie AI-made image of a polar bear has circulated since 2023 with a caption calling it "a November 2026 meme" people would understand later. It came back as a singing AI video in late August, and now that November 2026 is here, people are posting it again. There is no real prediction behind it; it is collaborative internet fiction.

6. "What is a ground stop?" On Friday, Nov. 13, the FAA halted departures across the U.S. after a communications outage, and searches for the term jumped. A ground stop keeps flights at their departure airports until it is lifted. Full explainer: https://trendrundown.com/x/what-is-a-ground-stop
in_the_news: Our weekly roundup of what the internet talked about from Nov. 9 to Nov. 15, 2026.

faq.q: What was the biggest meme of the week?
faq.a: "Microsoft 364" and the Embassy of Finland in Canberra joke were the most widely shared, each with millions of views.

faq.q: Is the Fortnite Pirate Coin real?
faq.a: Yes. Epic Games confirmed the drop rate of about 1 in 137,500 chests, and the coin can drop until Dec. 5, 2026.

faq.q: Did anything happen in November 2026 like the polar bear meme said?
faq.a: No. The original post never made a real prediction; the meme is a running joke.

faq.q: How often is this list updated?
faq.a: Every Sunday, with the trends of the past seven days.
